openingQuery: Which one should I choose? Compare the two options using their current prices and availability.

chat.content: Which one should I choose? Compare the two options using their current prices and availability.

Choose the Santal & Fig Candle. It is the stronger morning-ritual gift from the two options already shown: $92 stays below your $100 ceiling, and Aurora still reports positive stock. The Ceramic Ring Dish remains eligible at $35, but the candle is the more substantial single gift.

plan.flowSummary: Dispatcher → Personalization Agent + the-gift-table → search_products_hybrid (two-product price and stock revalidation)

toolCalls.description: Revalidate the two prior candidates against price, stock, and the recorded hybrid ranks
toolCalls.sql:
SELECT product_id, name, price, quantity
FROM product_catalog
WHERE name IN ('Santal & Fig Candle', 'Ceramic Ring Dish')
  AND price <= 100
  AND quantity > 0
ORDER BY CASE name
  WHEN 'Santal & Fig Candle' THEN 1
  ELSE 2
END;
toolCalls.resultSummary: Both prior options remain eligible; Santal & Fig Candle selected at $92 with positive stock

memoryPills.content: Choose from the same two-product shortlist and prove budget plus stock
Recent searches mention 'for my mother'; bought a sundress as a birthday gift last month

telemetry.title: Intent → Personalization Agent
telemetry.description: 'which one' resolved against Anna's two-product shortlist

telemetry.title: Memory Recall – Semantic
telemetry.description: Loaded Anna's gift-buyer profile and the prior $100 ceiling from AgentCore Memory. Used to preserve the shortlist and decision criteria.

telemetry.title: Memory Recall – Episodic
telemetry.description: Read Aurora episodic memory: recent 'for my mother' searches and last month's birthday-gift sundress purchase. Strengthens gift framing.
telemetry.sql: SELECT event_type, content, ts FROM customer_episodic_seed WHERE customer_id = $1 ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 10;

telemetry.title: vector branch
telemetry.description: Recorded vector ranks for the two prior gift candidates
telemetry.sql:
SELECT product_id, name, 1 - (embedding <=> $1::vector) AS similarity
FROM product_catalog
WHERE quantity > 0
ORDER BY embedding <=> $1::vector
LIMIT 20;

telemetry.title: Postgres FTS branch
telemetry.description: Recorded morning-ritual and gift terms for the same candidates
telemetry.sql:
SELECT product_id, name, price, quantity, ts_rank_cd(description_tsv, q) AS text_rank
FROM product_catalog, to_tsquery('english', 'morning:* | ritual:* | gift:*') q
WHERE name IN ('Santal & Fig Candle', 'Ceramic Ring Dish')
  AND price <= 100
  AND quantity > 0
ORDER BY text_rank DESC;

telemetry.title: RRF merge
telemetry.description: Reconstructed the two-product shortlist from recorded vector and lexical ranks
telemetry.sql:
SELECT product_id, rrf_score
FROM rrf
ORDER BY rrf_score DESC
LIMIT 30;

sections.title: The decision
paragraphs: The response may choose only from the two products already shown. PostgreSQL revalidates the $100 ceiling and positive stock before the model explains why the candle is the stronger gift.
